Resolves #19885

A dock tab group whose tabs were reordered now shows its "More tabs" control again once its tabs overflow. On every retained-chrome move, `Reconciler.moveRetainedTabChrome` switched the tab bar's overflow control to `hideMode: 'visibility'`. That transport hold was written for the floating control (#17841). Two days later #17960 made the dock's control a toolbar action that is hidden by `removeDom` while every tab fits. After a reorder had switched its mode, the plugin's `show()` only cleared the visibility style, and the removed node never returned. A trace in the App Worker showed `hidden: false`, `vdom.removeDom: true` and `mounted: false` after the drop. Any reorder therefore cut that group's overflow control off for the rest of the session: narrowed to 600 px, four tabs were unreachable. The hold now applies only to a floating control, which mirrors the restore at the end of the same projection (`!plugin.projectAsAction && …`).

Evidence: L3 (a browser e2e case, red on base and green at head). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | The ticket's own sequence, re-run with headless Chrome against the fixed tree (splitter 180 px left, History to the front): the rail reads `More tabs, lock, reload, maximize, close` and the plugin's hidden set is Alerts. CI-covered for the menu and the pick: `DockTabOverflowNL.spec.mjs` "a reordered group still shows the control once its tabs overflow, and the menu reaches them" opens the control's menu and picks a hidden tab, which becomes the pressed, visible header. |
| AC-2 | Red on base: with only `Reconciler.mjs` reverted, the new case fails at "the overflowing group shows its control" (`element(s) not found`), and the existing case passes. Green at head: 6/6 with `--repeat-each=3`. |
| AC-3 | The new case expects no control at full width, both before and after the swap. The existing case's 1600 px leg still removes it. |

## Deltas from ticket

- The e2e drives the defect through a path that does not depend on fonts: one swap at full width (Strategy onto Swarm's centre, `DockDragDropNL`'s single-midpoint drag), then the viewport narrowed to 600 px. The ticket's splitter sequence depends on the 437 px tab width in macOS fonts, so it is the AC-1 row's local run, not the test.

## Test Evidence

- `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=<brain checkout> npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockTabOverflowNL.spec.mjs --repeat-each=3 --retries=0 --workers=1`: 6 passed at ad11eb42ba. Without the variable the spec is not selected, because the external-Brain filter matches the word `neuralLink` in its header comment (defect-note filed). The spec uses only `page`, and no Brain service starts.
- `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs unit/dashboard/ unit/apps/workstation/Workspace unit/examples/dashboard/`: 1493 passed, 2 skipped.

Per §9 Strategic-Fit Step-Back:
- **Decision**: Approve
- **Rationale**: Exact root-cause fix at `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs#moveRetainedTabChrome`: gating the `hideMode: 'visibility'` transport hold on `!overflow.projectAsAction` makes `moveRetainedTabChrome` symmetric with the post-projection restore at line 709 (`!plugin.projectAsAction && ...`), preventing action-mode (`removeDom`) overflow controls from having their `hideMode` silently flipped to `'visibility'` while unmounted (`vdom.removeDom: true`).

**Peer-Review Opening:** Great root-cause diagnosis, Ada! Tracing `hidden: false, vdom.removeDom: true, mounted: false` in the App Worker to `moveRetainedTabChrome`'s unconditional `setSilent({hideMode: 'visibility'})` explains why the control disappeared permanently after any tab reorder. Making the transport hold floating-only (`!overflow.projectAsAction`) aligns `moveRetainedTabChrome` with the restore pass at line 709.
